This synergistic tandem configuration delivers a urea production rate of 259.87 µg·gcat -1·h-1 under air, marking the first demonstration of photocatalytic urea synthesis from atmospheric CO2 and N2. In situ spectroscopic measurements and DFT calculations reveal that the imidazole-functionalized HTP segments act as hole-rich oxidation domains, promoting water oxidation to generate *OH species that oxidize locally enriched N2 to *NO intermediates. Simultaneously, the Cu3 clusters serve as electron-rich centers for CO adsorption and activation, forming *CO that couples with *NO via the critical *OCNO intermediate toward urea formation. This work not only showcases the first photocatalytic urea synthesis from air but also establishes a modular paradigm for cascade catalysts that integrate capture and conversion toward sustainable chemical transformations.

articles.title: Cation-Framework-Preserving Oxygen-Vacancy Engineering for Broadband Infrared Emission in High-Entropy Spinel Oxides.
articles.abstract: NA: High-temperature radiative ceramics require broadband infrared emission and stable structures, but the defects that enhance emission can also weaken oxide lattices. Here, we regulate oxygen vacancies in (MnCrFeNiCu)3O4, a high-entropy spinel oxide (HEO), by vacuum annealing without changing the nominal cation composition. This approach regulates oxygen nonstoichiometry without introducing an additional cation-substitution variable. The binary Mn-Cr reference has band-averaged emissivities of 0.668 and 0.726 over 0.78-2.5 and 2.5-16 µm, respectively. Pristine HEO increases these values to 0.919 and 0.863, while the optimized HEO-OV-5 h reaches 0.932 and 0.902. Multication incorporation broadens electronic states near the band edges. Oxygen removal creates vacancy-derived states, redistributes charge, and changes local M─O coordination. The vacancy-derived states are consistent with localized d-d excitation, intervalence charge transfer, and polaron-related absorption, while changes in M─O coordination broaden vibrational absorption. Together, these electronic and local structural changes are consistent with the enhanced infrared emissivity. The spinel framework and high emissivity remain largely preserved after annealing at 1000°C for 5 h. These results show that oxygen vacancies can be regulated within a stable multication spinel to combine broadband infrared emission with high-temperature stability.

articles.title: "Water-in-Water" Biphasic Electrolyte for Aqueous Zinc-ion Batteries.
articles.abstract: NA: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) are constrained by unstable Zn metal interfaces, where nonuniform Zn2+ transport induces concentration polarization and accelerates parasitic reactions. Here we show that Zn2+ flux can instead be regulated by aqueous-aqueous interfaces. A fully aqueous "water-in-water" (W/W) biphasic electrolyte, comprising dextran (Dex)-rich phase droplets (∼10 µm) suspended in a polyethylene glycol (PEG)-rich aqueous phase, creates phase boundaries that continuously buffer local Zn2+ accumulation and redistribute ions during plating and stripping. As a result, Zn||Zn cells cycle stably for 1100 h at 10 mA cm-2 and 10 mAh cm-2, and Ah-level Zn||NaV3O8 pouch cells sustain long-term operation. This work demonstrates an aqueous electrolyte architecture in which interfacial electrostatics, rather than solvent chemistry, governs Zn2+ transport.

articles.title: From Dark Photocatalysis to Photobattery-Type Operation: A Re-Functionalized Ti-MOF for Solar Energy Storage.
articles.abstract: NA: Efficient harvesting, storage, and on-demand release of solar energy are essential for overcoming the intermittency of sunlight and enabling continuous solar energy-driven processes, yet achieving storage of photogenerated charge remains challenging. Here, we report a Ti-based bipyridine MOF, COK47-bpy, and its ReCl(CO)3-functionalized analogue, ReCl47-bpy, as photochargeable materials for time-decoupled solar energy utilization. Re incorporation introduces localized photosensitizing and "electron sink" sites while preserving the parent framework structure, enabling visible-light response, faster charge accumulation, and improved charge retention. In colloidal suspension, ReCl47-bpy reaches an electron storage capacity of 19.5 C g-1 MOF under simulated solar irradiation and retains about 70% of the stored charge after 2.5 months. The stored electrons can be released on demand for dark hydrogen (H2) evolution with electron-to-H2 efficiencies exceeding 90%. Beyond colloids, when fabricated as robust FTO-supported layers, ReCl47-bpy|FTO photoelectrodes deliver capacities of up to ∼7.0 mAh g-1 MOF upon photocharging under 1 Sun irradiation. Overall, this work establishes Re-functionalized Ti-MOFs as versatile platforms for solar-driven charge storage, dark photocatalysis, and MOF-based photoelectrodes, toward the development of next-generation MOF-based energy devices.

articles.title: Cyclic Nonequilibrium Processing of Halide Solid Electrolytes for Low-Pressure Operation of all-Solid-State Batteries.
articles.abstract: NA: Sluggish ionic transport and high rigidity of inorganic solid electrolytes (SSEs) necessitate ultra-high external pressures in all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), posing a major barrier to their deployment. Herein, we propose a cyclic nonequilibrium thermal process for Li3InCl6 (LIC) solid electrolyte, which is implemented through repeated quenching to concurrently optimize ionic transport and deformability. The initial quench refines particle size, whereas subsequent quenching induces local amorphization, thereby suppressing grain boundary resistance and enhancing compressibility. Meanwhile, additional Li vacancies are introduced, accelerating bulk phase ionic transport. These coupled mesoscopic and microscopic structural evolutions increase the room-temperature ionic conductivity (IC) of LIC from 1.3 to 6.8 mS/cm, while reducing the Young's modulus from 42.3 to 17.6 GPa. The optimized LIC enables a stable cycling of ASSBs at a low operation pressure of 2 MPa with a high areal capacity of 7.7 mAh/cm2, highlighting cyclic nonequilibrium processing as a promising route for practical ASSBs.

articles.title: Advances in Bio-Integrated Edge Computing Systems for Smart and Connected Health.
articles.abstract: NA: Recent advances in bio-integrated healthcare technologies have enabled continuous, high-resolution monitoring and active therapeutic intervention through wearable, implantable, and ingestible platforms. In parallel, edge computing has emerged as a critical framework for processing biomedical data locally, enabling low-latency, energy-efficient, and privacy-preserving operation. This review provides a comprehensive overview of bio-integrated edge computing systems for smart and connected health, focusing on the co-design of computing, sensing, and energy strategies. We first examine computing approaches, including conventional von Neumann architectures and emerging paradigms such as compute-in-memory and neuromorphic systems, for on-device data processing and decision-making. We then discuss sensing strategies that enhance signal fidelity and enable efficient information representation at the biointerface. Finally, we review energy solutions that enable continuous, autonomous operation. By integrating these domains, this work outlines pathways toward scalable, adaptive, and fully autonomous edge healthcare systems.

articles.title: Rare-Earth-Cluster-Mediated Long-Range Electronic Modulation Activates Zn Atomic Sites for Oxygen Reduction Catalysis.
articles.abstract: NA: Activating the inert Zn (d10) centers via precise ligand-field engineering to achieve superior oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) performance is highly appealing yet challenging. Herein, we report a general long-range electronic structure regulation strategy to construct ultrafine rare-earth oxide clusters anchored proximal to Zn single-atom sites (LaOx-Zn-SA/CNCl), aiming at boosting ORR activity. Benefiting from the tailored long-range electronic modulation by LaOx clusters and the hierarchical porous carbon support that maximizes Zn atom utilization, the catalysts exhibit a high half-wave potential of 0.90 V along with remarkable stability in alkaline media. This represents a non-precious-metal, rare-earth-based electrocatalyst among the best reported so far. A zinc-air battery (ZAB) integrating LaOx-Zn-SA/CNCl as the cathode catalyst delivers a maximum power density of 177.3 mW cm-2 at 225 mA cm-2. Theoretical calculations reveal that the proximal LaOx clusters remotely modulate the electronic structures of Zn sites, enhancing electron-transfer efficiency by strengthening electronic interactions. With the optimized electronic state of Zn sites, the adsorption of key intermediates is balanced to alleviate the energy barriers of the rate-determining step. This work provides insights into the long-range electronic regulation of transition-metal single-atom sites within a hierarchical rare-earth cluster-coupled microenvironment for efficient electrocatalysis.

articles.title: Hypoxia-Tolerant Supramolecular Nanomicelles for Pyroptosis-Enhanced NIR-II Phototheranostics.
articles.abstract: NA: Tumor hypoxia, limited solid-tumor imaging, and insufficient systemic antitumor immunity remain major challenges to effective cancer phototheranostics. Here, a molecular conformation engineering strategy is developed to construct TBBP, which features a strengthened electron donor, a moderately twisted conformation, extended π-conjugation, and a robust molecular skeleton free of labile olefinic π-bridges. TBBP exhibits excellent photostability, broadband second near-infrared (1000-1600 nm) emission, and efficient photothermal conversion (42.17%). Supramolecular assembly with DSPE-PEG2000 affords stable TBBP nanomicelles, TBBP NPs, that selectively generate superoxide radicals (O2 -•) and retain potent Type I photodynamic therapy (PDT) activity under hypoxia. Photoactivated TBBP NPs further induce mitochondrial dysfunction and caspase-3/GSDME-mediated immunogenic pyroptosis, promoting dendritic cell maturation and CD8+ T cell infiltration. In a bilateral 4T1 tumor model, TBBP NPs enable high-contrast second near-infrared (NIR-II) imaging, while synergistic Type I PDT and photothermal therapy elicit systemic antitumor immunity, achieving 92.0% primary tumor inhibition and 47.7% distant tumor inhibition. This work establishes a molecular conformation engineering strategy and extends its functionality through supramolecular assembly, synergistically integrating NIR-II imaging, hypoxia-tolerant Type I phototherapy, and photoimmunotherapy, thereby providing a generalizable molecular design principle for the development of next-generation multifunctional organic phototheranostic agents.

articles.title: Boundary Guided Liquid-Bridge Adhesion for Robotic Pick-and-Release.
articles.abstract: NA: Liquid-bridge-mediated adhesion provides conformal contact with rough surfaces and gentle interaction with fragile microstructures, making it attractive for object manipulation. However, controlling liquid-bridge formation and retraction under non-ideal interfacial conditions remains challenging. Here, we report a switchable liquid-bridge adhesion strategy using a two-tiered stamp with spatially patterned wettability. Boundary-guided pinning confines liquid spreading to form a stable bridge for pickup and guides liquid retraction toward bridge breakup for controlled release. This design converts liquid-bridge adhesion from an uncontrolled capillary phenomenon into a controllable interfacial mechanism. The strategy enables preload-free adhesion switching, tunable adhesion forces, robust manipulation across surfaces with diverse roughness and wettability, and damage-free contact with fragile microstructures. Integrated with a robotic platform, the stamp functions as a liquid-bridge-based robotic end effector for pick-and-place manipulation and robotic placement, providing a route toward ultra-gentle manufacturing and microelectronic assembly.

articles.title: High-Performance Low Threshold Voltage n-Type OECTs via a Stepwise Cyanation of Quinoxaline-Based Polymeric Semiconductor.
articles.abstract: NA: Achieving both low threshold voltage (Vth) and high performance in organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) is critical for low-power, high-sensitivity bioelectronics, yet simultaneously achieving low Vth and high device performance remains a long-standing challenge. Herein, we propose a stepwise cyanation strategy to modify quinoxaline-based polymeric semiconductors to mitigate this dilemma. Benefiting from the strong electron-withdrawing ability of cyano substituents, QxCN-CNTVT functionalized with cyano groups on both donor and acceptor units exhibits a deep LUMO level of -4.23 eV, one of the deepest among reported n-type ionic-electronic conductors. As a result, OECTs based on QxCN-CNTVT demonstrate excellent comprehensive performance, with a high µC* value of up to 168.89 F cm-1 V-1 s-1 and a low Vth of 0.13 V, while maintaining superior operational stability (retaining ∼80% of the initial current after 10,000 s of continuous operation and 10,000 full switching cycles). Furthermore, QxCN-CNTVT is successfully applied to complementary inverters for efficient amplification of electrooculogram (EOG) and electrocardiogram (ECG) signals, as well as NAND and NOR logic gates for integrated logic functions. This work not only alleviates the widely observed imbalance between performance and Vth in n-type OECTs but also provides a versatile molecular design strategy for next-generation low-power bioelectronic devices.

articles.title: A Critical Call for Mechanistic Investigations of Metal-Bacteria Interactions.
articles.abstract: NA: The antibacterial properties of metals have been recognized for millennia. It is thus well established that this antibacterial response has tremendous importance for bioengineering applications, driving ever-increasing resources for research efforts, especially over the last few decades. What is less appreciated across the thousands of scientific investigations that appear in the literature, however, is the reproducibility crisis stemming from various challenging aspects of this research. In this perspective, we highlight this reproducibility problem, discuss its sources, and suggest solutions towards focused, mechanistic, interdisciplinary investigations. To make these recommendations operational, we provide a source-specific experimental roadmap, identify priority mechanistic questions with concrete investigation pathways, and highlight representative studies that combine causal perturbations, orthogonal measurements, and cross-laboratory validation.

articles.title: Layered Spin-Crossover Metal-Organic Frameworks for Light-Induced Control of Two-Dimensional Quantum Materials.
articles.abstract: NA: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are widely explored for gas separation, catalysis, or energy storage, yet their integration with other electronically functional materials remains largely unexplored. Here, we integrate the layered Hofmann-type spin-crossover (SCO) MOF {FeII(pyS2Et)2[PtII(CN)4]} into electrical nanodevices to control the properties of two-dimensional (2D) quantum materials. Our molecular approach exploits the stimuli-responsive nature of SCO-layered materials as switchable building blocks. We demonstrate selective modulation of the electronic transport in van der Waals heterostructures interfacing SCO with 2D quantum materials (few-layer graphene, magnetic CrSBr, superconducting NbSe2) through the strain induced via thermal and light-induced spin transitions. In graphene, the conductivity is selectively switched by light. In spin-valves based on CrSBr bilayers, the MOF triggers magnetic hysteresis (absent in pristine CrSBr) and enables tunable non-volatile zero-field memory. In NbSe2, light modulates the superconducting critical current and transition temperature. These results establish layered stimuli-responsive SCO MOFs as active molecular control elements for 2D quantum materials, providing a route to strain-mediated control of electronic, magnetic, and superconducting functionalities, and extending MOF-based architectures beyond traditional porous-matter applications toward multifunctional electronics and spintronics.

articles.title: Directional Confinement Governed Ion Transport for Efficient Actuation.
articles.abstract: NA: Ionic transport kinetics in electrolytes are a key determinant of ionic actuator performance. Conventional random porous electrolytes are constrained by porosity and tortuosity, leading to an intrinsic limitation in ion mobility within the Bruggeman framework. Here, structural anisotropy is introduced to establish a unified framework that analyzes ion transport from random diffusion to directionally confined regimes. To validate this concept, anisotropic electrolytes with oriented channels are fabricated via directional freeze-drying. These structures exhibit pronounced directional dependence, with through-plane ion mobility twice higher than that of the disordered counterparts, leading to significantly enhanced ionic actuator performance and mitigating the inherent trade-off between strain and blocking force. Moreover, the directional confinement effect is observed across multiple polymer systems, highlighting the critical role of structural anisotropy in regulating ion transport and offering a framework for enhancing electrolyte performance through microstructural design. This strategy enables environmentally robust and stable operation of soft electrochemical actuators for grippers and biomimetic robotics.

articles.title: Dual Twisted Interfaces Enable Tunable Second Harmonic Generation in Chemical Vapor Deposition Grown Trilayer MoS2.
articles.abstract: NA: Twisted bilayer transition metal dichalcogenides, governed by a single twisted interface, offer a versatile platform for manipulating interlayer coupling and emergent optical behavior. However, despite extensive studies on single twisted interface systems, how multi-interface twisted stacking influences nonlinear optical behavior remains unclear. Here, we address this gap by systematically investigating the nonlinear optical performance of chemical vapor deposition (CVD) grown twisted trilayer MoS2 (TT-MoS2) with multi-interface twisted stacking. We fabricate all nine distinct trilayer MoS2 configurations by CVD. Raman and photoluminescence show that twisted interfaces modulate interlayer coupling, giving rise to stacking-dependent phonon and excitonic responses. Atomic-resolution scanning, transmission electron microscopy, and selected area electron diffraction confirm dual twisted interfaces and a supermoiré lattice. Guided by these structural insights, we examine the second harmonic generation (SHG) response across all nine trilayer configurations. Extending the coherent SH field superposition model to a trilayer system with two independent twisted interfaces, we develop a framework that describes how the dual interfaces govern the SHG intensity and polarization orientation across stacking configurations. Our findings establish TT-MoS2 as a versatile nonlinear platform and open new avenues for understanding and exploiting multi-interface twisted coupling to engineer nonlinear optical responses in van der Waals materials.

articles.title: Solvation-Equilibrium Locking Enables Ultrawide-Temperature Operation of High-Voltage Lithium-Metal Batteries.
articles.abstract: NA: High-energy lithium metal batteries are promising for space, polar, deep-sea, and other extreme environments, but their operation is constrained by temperature-sensitive ion transport, Li+ solvation, and interfacial chemistry. A solvation-equilibrium-locked electrolyte (SELE) is reported by combining dimethyl sulfite (DMS), a low-freezing weakly solvating solvent, with Pyr13DFOB (1-methyl-1-propylpyrrolidinium difluoro(oxalato)borate) as an ionic-liquid co-solvent. Cooperative ion-dipole and weak C-H⋯O interactions between DMS and Pyr13 + regulate the free-solvent reservoir, while TFSI- (bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide) and DFOB- enrich the primary Li+ coordination shell. Variable-temperature 7Li NMR, Raman, and molecular dynamics simulations show that solvent-separated ion pairs, contact ion pairs, and aggregates remain nearly invariant from -60°C to 60°C, unlike the strongly temperature-responsive Pyr13DFOB-free electrolyte. This locked anion-rich solvation structure reduces solvent coordination around Li+, mitigates solvent-derived interfacial decomposition and gas evolution, and promotes LiF- and borate-rich interphases on Li metal and NMC811. Consequently, Li||NMC811 cells deliver discharge capacity at -85°C and operate up to 120°C, while pouch cells remain functional after cooling to -122.9°C. A 6.6 Ah Li||Ni90 pouch cell further achieves 565 Wh kg-1 under lean-electrolyte conditions, establishing solvation-equilibrium locking as a molecular design principle for lithium metal batteries operating over a broad temperature range.

articles.title: Thickness-Defined Transport Regime Toward Near-Ideal Area-Type Switching.
articles.abstract: NA: Area-type memristors are attractive for analog in-memory computing, but their use is often limited by parasitic charge storage, causing readout drift, non-pinched hysteresis, and degraded readout fidelity. We show that near-ideal area-type switching emerges within a tunneling-governed transport regime in ultrathin layers that suppresses charging-related readout artifacts. By varying the thickness in TiN/Ta2O5/Pt in a range of 3-10 nm, we reveal the transition from filamentary switching to near-short-circuit transport with two gradual-switching modes with different readout stability. The 5-6 nm thickness window suppresses non-pinched hysteresis and short-time drift while preserving analog switching, yielding nearly polarity-symmetric hysteresis and readout, clear area scaling, and continuous near-linear conductance modulation. Our analysis indicates that trap-assisted tunneling dominates the stabilized-state response, whereas ionic redistribution governs pristine-state reconstruction and the stability boundaries. A compact model is derived for the 5 nm device which reproduces the quasi-static I-V behavior and the dynamic resistance evolution based on pulse-width-dependent characteristics. The verified model is provided as Verilog-A code enabling simulation in circuit design tools. Our results demonstrate that ultrathin scaling is a regime-defining design rule for near-ideal area-type operation in oxide memristors, implying a fundamental approach to fabricating robust multi-state memristors for in-memory computing applications.

articles.title: Synthesis of Bulk Superconducting LiNbO2 Crystals Through CaH2 Reduction.
articles.abstract: NA: We have synthesized layered superconducting LiNbO2 crystals through a bulk phase transformation from LiNbO3 single crystals via CaH2 reduction. As the Nb valence is reduced from 5+ to 3+, the material undergoes a structural transformation to the resulting product, LiNbO2, which is accompanied by metallic behavior and a superconducting transition, Tc onset, as high as 14.4 K. Secondary ion mass spectroscopy (SIMS) and x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) show that the resulting phase is hole-doped through de-lithiation during the reduction. Magnetization and AC susceptibility measurements from a tunnel diode resonator confirm the bulk nature of superconductivity with a superconducting volume fraction of ≈77% and an upper critical field approaching 26 T. Our study demonstrates extreme hydride reduction as an effective method to induce phase transformations with non-topochemical pathways and can be used to synthesize bulk materials with exotic properties.

articles.title: Voltage Hysteresis Induced by Fragile Quasi-Flat Bands in Oxygen-Redox Cathodes.
articles.abstract: NA: Cathodes exploiting oxygen redox chemistry underpin the realization of lithium battery systems with specific energies beyond 600 Wh kg-1. However, voltage hysteresis exceeding 1 V, especially during the first cycle, remains a long-standing and unresolved challenge, severely limiting energy efficiency and practical deployment. Here, we propose a quasi-flat-band framework in which oxygen 2p states near the Fermi level are intrinsically sensitive to perturbations. Even weak perturbations, such as minor lattice distortions during delithiation or thermal vibrations at room temperature, can disproportionately amplify band dispersion and induce hysteresis. This insight reframes the long-standing design strategy by extending it beyond suppressing structural reconstructions to include control of perturbation-driven electronic instability. Future materials design should pursue two principles: stabilizing symmetry to sustain quasi-flat-band characteristics and engineering orbital hybridization to enhance their robustness against perturbations. This work rethinks the origin and mitigation of voltage hysteresis, bringing oxygen-redox cathodes closer to reliable operation at high voltages.

articles.title: Axial Benzotriazole-Coordinated Ni Single Atoms Enable Rapid Interfacial Electron Transfer for Efficient Photocatalytic Acetylene Semi-Hydrogenation.
articles.abstract: NA: Photocatalytic semi-hydrogenation of acetylene (C2H2) to ethylene (C2H4) often suffers from inefficient interfacial electron transfer from the photocatalysts to adsorbed C2H2. Here, we demonstrate that axial coordination of benzotriazole (BTA) to Ni single atoms in C3N4 (BTA-Ni SAs-C3N4) facilitates interfacial electron-transfer processes. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, in situ transient surface photovoltage spectroscopy, in situ photochemical infrared spectroscopy, and theoretical simulations reveal that BTA-coordinated Ni SAs serve as the centers for rapid electron transfer by upshifting the Ni d-band center and strengthening the orbital overlap between Ni SA and adsorbed C2H2. Consequently, BTA-Ni SAs-C3N4 achieves a very high C2H4 production rate of 32.29 mmol gcat -1 h-1 with a C2H4 selectivity of 97.6% under simulated solar irradiation, which is ∼4-times higher than that for Ni SAs-C3N4. The apparent quantum yield at 365 nm is up to 4.65%, superior to reported photocatalytic acetylene semi-hydrogenation. This work highlights the importance of interfacial charge transfer in photocatalytic acetylene hydrogenation and provides a rational strategy for designing high-performance photocatalysts.

articles.title: Radiative Cooling Floating Covers Cool Lakes and Suppress Evaporation.
articles.abstract: NA: Globally, warmer lakes disrupt thermal balance, causing hypoxia, salinization, biodiversity loss, and increased evaporation. Conventional floating covers used to reduce evaporation absorb sunlight and warm the underlying water, limiting suppression efficiency to less than the coverage ratio (ηeff/Φ ≤ 1). Here, we break this limit by developing Superhydrophobic Radiative Cooling Covers (SRCC) via multi-level structural design. SRCC actively cools the water surface by combining high solar reflectance, strong mid-infrared emission, and superhydrophobicity. Experiments show SRCC lowers water temperature by 2.2°C versus uncovered water, achieving 93.1± 0.1% evaporation suppression at 91% coverage, yielding ηeff/Φ > 1.0 for the first time. Large‑scale simulations for nine Chinese lakes indicate that SRCC reduces water temperature by 4.87°C (vs. no cover) and by 12.44 °C (vs. black covers). This cooling could increase annual freshwater reserves by 10.78 km3 across China under full deployment, equivalent to 20.9 L per person per day. Unattainable with conventional covers, SRCC uniquely mitigates thermal accumulation while enhancing freshwater storage, providing a quantifiable engineering solution to climate‑driven water stress and enabling adaptive lake ecosystem management across regional and global scales.

articles.title: Correction to "Screening Natural Cholesterol Analogs to Assemble Self-Adjuvant Lipid Nanoparticles for Antigens Tagging Guided Therapeutic Tumor Vaccine".
Synchronized Ablation of Multifocal Tumors Enabled by Multi-Channel Lanthanide Nanocomposites.
articles.abstract: NA: The multifocal nature of orthotopic breast tumors makes it difficult to treat due to individual tumor differences, requiring multiple therapeutic interventions. Here, a customized therapeutic strategy is presented for multiple tumors by using the same prescription based on a multi-channel lanthanide nanocomposite and orthogonally controlled drug release. The upconversion luminescence of the nanocomposite at different wavelengths can monitor pH-responsive mitoxantrone (MXT) release, reduced glutathione-responsive near-infrared (NIR) absorbance change, and eigen temperature, respectively, allowing modulation of photothermal treatment and temperature-responsive paclitaxel release through customized whole-body irradiation to achieve synchronized ablation of different individual tumors. Small animal experiments confirm multifocal breast tumors can be treated through this customized therapeutic strategy with both high efficiency and low overtherapy risk.

articles.title: Anatomically Accessible Local mRNA Therapeutics: From Anatomical Access to Disease-Focused Applications.
articles.abstract: NA: Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics have expanded from clinically validated prophylactic vaccines toward protein replacement and supplementation. Yet mRNA delivery remains centered on intramuscular vaccination and intravenous administration, largely optimized for systemic adaptive immunity or circulation-mediated biodistribution. Many localized diseases, however, are confined to tissues or compartments accessible by topical, transdermal, inhaled, oral, catheter-based, ocular, or intra-articular administration without initial reliance on circulation. For these diseases, the therapeutic objective is likewise local: therapeutically relevant mRNA expression occurs within the affected tissue, and efficacy derives predominantly from the local biological activity of the encoded protein rather than from downstream systemic effects initiated by local expression. This therapeutic paradigm is defined here as Anatomically Accessible Local mRNA Therapeutics (ALmT). The review first distinguishes ALmT from intravenous mRNA delivery and intramuscular mRNA vaccination, then organizes site-specific barriers and engineering strategies across major anatomical sites. It further examines disease-focused ALmT applications, highlighting protein restoration, cytokine or growth-factor supplementation, local antibody-fragment production, regenerative modulation, and tissue repair. Finally, it discusses general design principles, quantitative PK/PD evaluation, repeat-dose safety, and clinical translation. Overall, the ALmT framework may facilitate the design, quantitative evaluation, and clinical translation of mRNA therapies for localized diseases.

articles.title: Beyond Facet Engineering: Dislocation-Mediated Nucleation Enables Stable Lithium Deposition on Practical Polycrystalline Cu Collectors.
articles.abstract: NA: Uniform Li deposition on practical Cu current collectors remains challenging in lithium metal batteries. Despite extensive efforts in facet engineering, achieving homogeneous Li deposition on practical polycrystalline Cu collectors remains elusive, highlighting an incomplete understanding of the structural factors governing Li deposition. Herein, a defect-mediated interfacial engineering strategy is developed by simultaneously introducing a high density of geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) and enriched <110>/<111> textures on commercial electrodeposited Cu foils. Theoretical calculations and experiments reveal that densely distributed dislocations provide thermodynamically favorable Li adsorption sites and abundant preferential heterogeneous nucleation sites, while the enriched <110>/<111> textures promote Li surface diffusion and lateral growth. This combined effect promotes uniform and compact initial Li deposition, guiding path-dependent deposition evolution and suppressing interfacial heterogeneity. The control experiments further support a key contribution of dislocation defects, while variations in surface chemistry or morphology alone cannot account for the observed performance differences. The optimized Cu foil sustains over 1200 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.52% ± 0.20% over the final 200 cycles (n = 4) in Li||Cu cells and improves N/P = 0 Cu||NCM811 full-cell cycling. This work establishes dislocation-mediated nucleation and orientation-regulated growth as a design principle for practical Cu current collectors.

articles.title: Nonreciprocal Bending in Ferroelectric Membranes Driven by Flexoelectricity.
articles.abstract: NA: Nonreciprocity reflects the asymmetric propagation or motion of an object in two opposite directions and can achieve directional transport in physics. However, nonreciprocity in natural quasi-static mechanical systems, including nonreciprocal bending, has rarely been explored. Here we demonstrate nonreciprocal bending in a freestanding ferroelectric single-crystalline PbTiO3 membrane using suspended-membrane nanoindentation. The mechanical bending of the ferroelectric membrane is strongly asymmetric in the two opposite bending directions with a difference in effective elastic modulus of up to 33%. The elastic recovery of bending deformation also becomes polarity-dependent. Such unconventional nonreciprocal bending originates from the asymmetric ferroelectric domain switching driven by the crucial flexoelectricity, as revealed by phase-field simulations. This work enriches the nonreciprocal functionalities of ferroelectrics and presents a route for exploring more nonreciprocal effects by flexoelectric engineering.

articles.title: Ordered Crystallographic Orientation of Dion-Jacobson 2D Perovskites for Ultrastable Solar Cells.
articles.abstract: NA: Dion-Jacobson (DJ) 2D perovskites show great potential in stability but do not meet theoretical expectations for photovoltaics due to the random crystallographic orientation in films. We herein report ordered crystallographic orientation of the DJ 2D perovskite, achieved by modifying the intermediate-phase film with a Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) phase 2D perovskite based on the two-step processing method. The introduction of the RP 2D perovskite lowers the energy barrier for the transition from the intermediate phase to the 2D perovskite phase with the ordered alignment, and this strategy is applicable to various organic diammoniums-based DJ 2D perovskites. Solar cells with oriented DJ 2D perovskite films achieve an efficiency of 21.1% (19.05% for 1 cm2 devices) and exhibit outstanding stability by retaining 98.1% of initial efficiency after 2000 h of maximum power point tracking at 65°C under continuous 1-sun illumination (ISOS-L-2 protocol) and 98.7% after 2500 h testing at a relative humidity of 85%.

articles.title: All-In-One Integration of Inherently Flame-Retardant, UV-Resistant, and Antibacterial Polymer by a Biguanide Unit.
articles.abstract: NA: The increasing fire accidents, excessive UV exposure, and health threats posed by bacterial infections urgently require advanced polymer materials integrating multiple safety protections. In this study, we propose an ultra-efficient strategy to achieve the all-in-one integration of inherently flame-retardant, UV-resistant, and antibacterial polymer materials through a single biguanide unit. The key lies in the unique triple protection mechanism exerted by the biguanide unit: high-temperature char-formation for flame retardance, n→π* transition absorption for UV-resistance, and disruption of the negatively charged bacterial surface for antibacteria. As a result, the biguanide-containing polymer material achieves the best UL-94 V-0 flame-retardant rating with excellent self-extinguishing properties, ≥99.3% ultra-high shielding rate for UV light, and ≥99.0% remarkable antibacterial rate. Importantly, the biguanide unit is chemically bonded to the polymer main chain, which not only avoids the health risks and performance degradation caused by the additive migration, but also exhibits outstanding heat resistance, thermal stability, and easy processability. This work simultaneously achieves triple functional integration of polymer materials through a single biguanide unit, realizing previously unattainable multiple safety protections against dangerous fires, harmful UV, and widely-existed bacteria.

articles.title: Magnetic-Field-Annealing-Induced Short-Range Order in High-Entropy Alloys for Enhanced Electromagnetic Response.
articles.abstract: NA: The growing demand for microwave absorbers in 5G/6G technologies motivates processing routes that balance matching thickness, attenuation, and temperature response. Here, magnetic field annealing (MFA) is investigated in rGO-supported FeCoNi, FeCoNiCr, and FeCoNiCrCu compositionally complex alloys at 0, 0.5, and 0.95 T. Among the investigated FeCoNiCr samples, the 0.5 T sample exhibits a favorable combination of dielectric and magnetic responses. Reflection loss yields a minimum of -72.30 dB at 1.59 mm, and a maximum effective absorption bandwidth of 4.40 GHz. At 85°C, the maximum bandwidth is 4.08 GHz, corresponding to 92.7% retention of temperature-specific maxima. Local microscopy, field-associated atomistic modeling, and fixed-composition electronic-structure calculations support an interpretation of the electromagnetic response in terms of Co-centered chemical correlations. Finally, flexible antennas and strain sensors based on this composite demonstrate stable wearable responses, validating this SRO strategy from atomic design to device integration.

articles.title: Pathway Engineering Enables Durable Iridium-Free Acidic Water Oxidation.
articles.abstract: NA: The pursuit of noble metal-free alternatives to iridium for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is critically impeded by a pervasive activity-stability trade-off, wherein non-precious metals undergo rapid oxidative dissolution under operating potentials. Here, we report a lutetium-stabilized cobalt oxide catalyst (Lu0.08Co2.92O4) designed through site-specific electronic modulation, achieving a synergistic enhancement of both activity and stability in acidic OER for proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs). Operando spectroscopies combined with theoretical simulations reveal that Lu incorporation introduces robust Lu-O bonds and induces charge redistribution that strengthens Co-O covalency and suppresses Co2+ dissolution, which is critical for improved OER durability, and simultaneously optimizes the Co-Co distance to favor direct O-O radical coupling with a reduced energy barrier. Leveraging these structural advantages, a practical PEMWE employing Lu0.08Co2.92O4 delivers an industrially relevant current density of 1000 mA cm-2 at 1.837 V. Separately, it maintains stable operation for over 900 h under a stepwise current density from 200 to 500 mA cm-2, highlighting its potential for sustainable hydrogen production.

articles.title: An Ultrarobust Dual-Modal Neural Fiber With In-Sensor Computing.
articles.abstract: NA: Touch behavior constitutes the most direct physical manifestation of human intentions, meaning that intention decoding requires human-machine interfaces to simultaneously sense touch position and pressure. Conventional systems, however, rely on physically stacked discrete sensors and von Neumann architectures, causing data redundancy and impaired wearability. Here, we present an in-sensor-computing dual-modal neural fiber (ID neural fiber) that overcomes this fundamental limitation. The ID neural fiber achieves an unprecedented position resolution of < 5 mm and a pressure detection limit of 0.6 N, combined with exceptional robustness-sustaining 300 times load-bearing capacity and exhibiting < 8% performance fluctuation under bending. Coupled with flexibility, waterproofing, and reconfigurability, the ID neural fiber can be seamlessly integrated into textiles for reliable operation in harsh environments, including underwater robotic control. Crucially, the ID neural fiber enables in-sensor computing that dramatically increases the information density and allows synchronized feature fusion through programmable logic gates, enabling efficient real-time intention recognition. To capture touch habits, an intelligent system with the ID neural fiber achieves a remarkable identification accuracy of 98.21%. This work establishes a new material-architecture paradigm that unifies ultrarobustness, dual-modality, and in-sensor computing, setting the stage for next-generation wearable human-machine interfaces with both comfort and intelligence.

articles.title: Turning Nd-Fe-B Swarf Into High-Value Bulk Feedstocks via Sustainable Hydrogen Plasma: From Rare-Earth Oxides to Metals and Hydrides.
articles.abstract: NA: Rare-earth permanent magnets (REPMs) are crucial for electric vehicles, wind turbines, and other high-efficiency electric motor systems. However, their production is energy-intensive, and global recycling rates are below 0.2%. Machining swarf is the main industrial waste from REPMs production. Despite its high rare-earth elements (REEs) content (∼20 wt.%), it has received limited attention for sustainable recycling. We introduce hydrogen plasma reduction (HPR) as a new environmentally friendly method to recover REEs from REPM swarf. By tuning the hydrogen content and treatment time, we achieve phase separation into metallic Fe and a Nd2O3-rich rare-earth fraction, providing a concentrated intermediate for subsequent REPM production. The process also enables direct rare-earth hydride formation, confirming the plasma-assisted partial rare-earth metallization in the molten state. This procedure turns REPM swarf into separated, high-value, high-purity feedstock in a single, acid-free step. Against the ∼70 kg CO2-eq kg-1 footprint of conventional REPM production, this recycling route offers a pathway toward substantially lower-emission magnet production while reducing reliance on primary REE supply.

articles.title: A Universal Spin-Polarization-Engineered Antibonding-Orbital Modulation Paradigm for Accelerating Reaction Kinetics in Ultrahigh-Rate Sodium-Ion Batteries.
articles.abstract: NA: Conversion-type anode materials hold great promise for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), yet their practical rate performance is fundamentally constrained by sluggish reaction kinetics beyond mass-transport limitations. Despite notable advances in accelerating ion/electron transport, intrinsically reducing the large reaction kinetic barrier and activation energy associated with robust metal-chalcogen (M─S) bonds remains a long-standing challenge. In this study, we propose a universal spin-polarization-engineered (SPE) antibonding-orbital modulation paradigm to fundamentally regulate M─S bond strength and enable ultrahigh-rate sodium storage. As a proof of concept, magnetic manganese heteroatom doping into heterojunctions enhances the saturation magnetization by ∼210%, inducing a spin-state transition from low-spin to high-spin configurations, which increases the electron occupation of antibonding orbitals formed between metal eg orbitals and chalcogen p orbitals, and thereby regulates M─S bond strength. Benefiting from this spin-engineered electronic reconstruction, Mn-FeS2/CoS2 anode delivers an ultrahigh-rate capability of 300 mA h g-1 at 120 A g-1, together with exceptional long-term durability (∼100% retention over 13 000 cycles at 100 A g-1), ranking among the best record. The generality of this strategy is further validated by extending SPE modulation to other magnetic dopants. Moreover, the industrial-level pouch cell is assembled to demonstrate the practical potential of this strategy.

articles.title: Nonlinear Electro-Optic Visible Photonic Circuits for Solid-State Quantum Defects.
articles.abstract: NA: Integrated visible photonic engines for solid-state quantum defects provide a foundation for scalable quantum networks. While miniaturization is advancing, active manipulation remains limited by the difficulty of achieving simultaneous milliwatt-scale visible light generation and high-contrast modulation. Despite extensive efforts, the concurrent chip-scale realization of nonlinear frequency conversion and fast temporal gating for high-fidelity quantum control has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate a monolithic thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) platform integrating periodically poled frequency conversion with GHz-bandwidth electro-optic (EO) switching. The device delivers off-chip green-light power exceeding 1 mW with an extinction ratio (ER) of 42.2 dB, enabling coherent spin control and time-resolved lifetime measurements of individual nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond through nanosecond gating. System performance is validated through pulsed optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR), Rabi oscillations, and Ramsey interference, supported by time-tagged photon counting with nanosecond resolution. By unifying sufficient nonlinear light generation with high-speed active manipulation, this platform establishes a scalable framework for the realization of high-rate quantum communication nodes.
